findings.reason: the declared graph omits the §5-before-§7 ordering the plan's own text requires, so two of §7's four nodes can be dispatched against files a sibling section is mid-write.
findings.text: §7 declares `depends-on` `s6` alone, yet its own mechanism (plan:225) requires the `cso-repair-and-check-families-fold` and `cso-resume-family-folds` nodes to wait on §5, because they write `reckon/crew/obligations.py` (also §5's, plan:242) and `reckon/mcp.py` (also §5's, plan:252), and §5 declares `depends-on` `s4`,`s6` (plan:24) so the graph orders neither before the other — a roadmap that releases §5 and §7 concurrently launches §7's third and fourth nodes against a `reckon/crew/obligations.py` and `reckon/mcp.py` that §5 still holds.

findings.reason: a deliverable the section asserts but no measure and no negative control covers cannot be reviewed or shown by the node's gate, so either a fifth check is added or the change moves to a node that measures it.
findings.text: §7's mechanism adds `widen` accepting any run that is not running and `complete --accept-path` writing the same fence record through `narrow_claim`/`release_claim` (plan:206-207), but §7's four done-when checks measure only tombstone output, successor parity, string-literal hygiene and the visible-leaf count (plan:262-277); no check drives `widen` on a non-running run or `complete --accept-path`, so that behaviour could regress with every gate green.
